    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Imports · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Imports/TicketRosterImportRunDTO.cs:8 · Level 1 · record

    • What it is: one committed roster import run (UC-48), as the upload component polls it: server-side progress (Processed of Total), the outcome counts so far, and on a failed run the machine-readable error code. It carries no ticket holder data (TicketRosterImportRunDTO.cs:3-7).
    • Depends on: TicketRosterImportStatus (hence Level 1), the TicketImportRunIdentifierType and EventIdentifierType aliases; ErrorCode holds one of TicketRosterImportErrorCodes.
    • Concept: a polled progress contract for long-running work. [Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability] assesses whether long operations leave the request path; the commit returns this DTO immediately and the client polls it while the background processor applies the roster in batches. [Rubric §19, State Management]: the client derives its "importing" state from the server's IsActive instead of keeping its own flag (TicketRosterUpload.razor.cs:85).
    • Walkthrough: RunId, EventId, Status, Total, Processed are required (TicketRosterImportRunDTO.cs:11,14,17,20,23). The outcome counts Added, Updated, Unchanged (erased holders included), Voided, Reinstated and LinkedExistingAccounts are optional ints (TicketRosterImportRunDTO.cs:26-41), since they fill in as the run proceeds. ErrorCode is nullable (TicketRosterImportRunDTO.cs:44). IsActive (TicketRosterImportRunDTO.cs:47) is a computed property: Status is Queued or Running, mirroring TicketImportRun.IsActive (TicketImportRun.cs:83).
    • Why it's built this way: the counts mirror TicketRosterImportResultDTO so the synchronous and the background paths report the same numbers; keeping IsActive on the contract puts the one definition of "still running" where both server and client read it.
    • Where it's used: mapped by TicketImportRunMapping; returned by StartTicketRosterImportHandler (StartTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:34,40) and GetTicketRosterImportHandler (GetTicketRosterImportHandler.cs:15,21); exposed by TicketRosterImportController (TicketRosterImportController.cs:38-39,129); polled by TicketRosterUpload (TicketRosterUpload.razor.cs:160,217).

    InsightCount

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.Tickets.Insights · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/Tickets/Insights/InsightCount.cs:15 · Level 0 · record

    • What it is: one count cell of a ticket insights report under the BR-278 small-number rule: a count of 1 or 2 is withheld, while 0 and 3 or more are reported exactly, so an aggregate can never single out one person (InsightCount.cs:3-8).
    • Depends on: nothing first-party; Math.Round with MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero from the BCL.
    • Concept introduced, server-side small-number suppression. [Rubric §30, Compliance/Privacy/Data Governance] assesses whether personal data is minimized and protected by design. Here the rule runs when the cell is created, in the factory, so a suppressed cell holds no number at all: neither the API response nor a CSV export ever carries the real value (InsightCount.cs:6-8). A client cannot un-hide what was never sent. [Rubric §9, API & Contract Design] assesses whether contracts make invalid states hard to express; the two factories are the only places that set the flag consistently with Count and Rate.
    • Walkthrough:
      • Constants: SmallNumberThreshold = 3 (InsightCount.cs:18) and SuppressedText = "fewer than 3" (:21), the text both the report UI and the CSV write in place of a withheld count.
      • State: Count is int?, null when suppressed (:24); IsSuppressed (:27); Rate is decimal? (:34), the count per unit of the cell's denominator (a 0-1 share for a percentage cell, a per-holder average for a total), rounded to four decimals.
      • Of(int count) (:39-42): suppressed cell when the count is small, else an exact cell with no rate.
      • Of(int count, int denominator) (:51-58): suppressed cell (rate suppressed with it) when small; otherwise Rate = count / denominator rounded to 4 places away from zero, and a zero or negative denominator yields 0 rather than a division error (:56).
      • IsSmall(int count) (:63): count is > 0 and < SmallNumberThreshold, so zero is deliberately exact.
    • Why it's built this way: zero carries no re-identification risk and "nobody did X" is useful to an organizer, so only 1 and 2 are withheld (InsightCount.cs:4-5,63). Suppressing the rate with the count closes the obvious back door of recomputing the count from rate times denominator (InsightCount.cs:11-12). The threshold is also reused outside the cell: the A6 domain list drops any company domain under it before taking the top ten (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/GetRosterInsightsHandler.cs:261-266).

TicketInsightsCsv writes SuppressedText for a withheld cell (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/Tickets/UseCases/GetTicketInsights/TicketInsightsCsv.cs:282,291); the UI displays it through InsightCountValue.     • Caveats / not-in-source: BR-278 itself is defined in the ADC specifications guide, not in code; the code is the only enforcement point verified here.

    BookmarkWriteOutcome

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.UserSessionBookmarks · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/UserSessionBookmarks/BookmarkWriteOutcome.cs:15 · Level 0 · record

    • What it is: the success value of a bookmark toggle: whether the write was confirmed by the server or kept on the device for later, and the new bookmark id when there is one.
    • Depends on: no first-party types; only the UserSessionBookmarkIdentifierType alias (the alias convention is taught in the primer).
    • Concept, "queued" is a success, not a failure. [Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity] assesses whether the app keeps working through a degraded dependency; here the degraded dependency is the attendee's own network. A star tapped with no signal is not an error the page must show: it is a write the device will deliver later, so it comes back as Result.Success with Queued: true rather than as a failure. [Rubric §19, State Management]: the page needs exactly two facts to settle its optimistic star, and this record carries exactly those two.
    • Walkthrough: a positional record with two members (BookmarkWriteOutcome.cs:15). Queued is true when the write was kept on the device to be sent when it is back online, or when it cancelled out an earlier queued write of the same session, and false when the server confirmed it (doc comment :6-10). BookmarkId is the server id after a confirmed add and null after a remove and after a queued add, "whose id the server has not assigned yet" (:11-14). The producer shows every combination: a confirmed add returns new BookmarkWriteOutcome(Queued: false, bookmark.Id) (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:110), an add that meets "already bookmarked" and a confirmed remove both return Queued: false, BookmarkId: null (:118, :129), and a successful enqueue returns Queued: true, BookmarkId: null (:211).
    • Why it's built this way: a null id after a duplicate add or a queued add is honest rather than lossy: the page keeps the star lit and resolves the id later, either on the next read or by session when the user un-stars it (the comment at SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:113-114). Keeping the record in .Shared lets Conference's pages read it without referencing Engagement's UI assembly, the same split ISessionBookmarkUIService relies on.
    • Where it's used: the return value of ISessionBookmarkUIService.SetBookmarkedAsync (ISessionBookmarkUIService.cs:62), produced by SessionBookmarkUIService and read by Conference's PublicSessionListView (PublicSessionListView.razor.cs:164, :186) and SessionBookmarkButton (SessionBookmarkButton.razor.cs:122).

    CreateBookmarkRequest

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.UserSessionBookmarks · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/UserSessionBookmarks/CreateBookmarkRequest.cs:6 · Level 0 · record

    • What it is: the two-field request body for "bookmark this session for this user". It is simultaneously the JSON contract of the POST /bookmarks endpoint and the CQRS command object the handler consumes; Engagement declares no separate internal command type for the create use case.
    • Depends on: no first-party types. It uses the two module-scoped identifier aliases UserIdentifierType and SessionIdentifierType (the alias convention is taught in the primer), which is why the type sits at Level 0.
    • Concept introduced, request-as-command. [Rubric §9, API & Contract Design] assesses whether the wire contract is explicit and stable; [Rubric §6, CQRS & Event-Driven] assesses whether writes flow through a command object and a single handler. Here the two collapse into one type on purpose: BookmarksController injects ICommandHandler<CreateBookmarkRequest, Result<UserSessionBookmarkDTO>> (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/Controllers/BookmarksController.cs:38) and passes the deserialized body straight into createHandler.HandleAsync(request, cancellationToken) (BookmarksController.cs:72), so there is no request-to-command mapping step to keep in sync. The trade-off is that the public contract and the command shape can no longer diverge, which is exactly what the module wants for a request this small.
    • Walkthrough: two members, both required and init-only. UserId (CreateBookmarkRequest.cs:9) names the owner of the bookmark; SessionId (CreateBookmarkRequest.cs:12) names the session being saved. required means neither construction nor JSON deserialization can leave a member unset, and init freezes the instance after construction, so no decorator in the CQRS pipeline can mutate a command mid-flight.
    • Why it's built this way: keeping the payload to two identifiers pushes every other concern to a dedicated place: shape validation to CreateBookmarkRequestValidator (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/UserSessionBookmarks/UseCases/Create/CreateBookmarkRequestValidator.cs:9), business rules (session validity, duplicate detection) to CreateBookmarkHandler (.../Create/CreateBookmarkHandler.cs:23), and authorization to the controller. Because UserId travels in the body rather than being inferred server-side, the controller binds it to the caller: a non-Organizer whose user-identifier claim does not equal request.UserId gets a Forbidden failure (BookmarksController.cs:58-70), the create-side counterpart of the OwnerOrAdminFilter on the list endpoints (ADR-033). [Rubric §11, Security]: without that check any authenticated user could create bookmarks owned by someone else. Note also the [Idempotent] attribute on the action (BookmarksController.cs:50), justified in the action's own doc comment (:45-47): because the body names the (user, session) pair explicitly and a duplicate already answers 409, replaying a retried star is what the attendee meant.
    • Where it's used: the API entry point CreateAsync (BookmarksController.cs:54-55); the UI HTTP wrapper BookmarkApiClient, whose CreateAsync takes one (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/BookmarkApiClient.cs:63-64); and SessionBookmarkUIService, which constructs one inline when a star is toggled online (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:140) and enqueues one as the offline-write payload when the device is offline (SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:201).

    IBookmarkCountService

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.UserSessionBookmarks · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/UserSessionBookmarks/IBookmarkCountService.cs:11 · Level 0 · interface

    • What it is: the cross-module read contract that lets Conference ask "how many people bookmarked this session?" without referencing an Engagement domain entity, an Engagement DbContext, or an Engagement package beyond .Shared.
    • Depends on: nothing first-party beyond the SessionIdentifierType alias and the ServiceContractAttribute marker it carries (IBookmarkCountService.cs:1, :10); BCL Task, IReadOnlyDictionary, IReadOnlyCollection, CancellationToken.
    • Concept introduced, the extraction-ready cross-module interface. [Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness] assesses whether modules talk through contracts that survive a process split; [Rubric §1, SOLID] (Dependency Inversion) assesses whether the consumer depends on an abstraction rather than a concrete collaborator. This interface is the canonical example in ADC: it has three different implementations that a host picks between with no consumer change at all. In-process it is BookmarkCountService (registered with TryAddScoped at MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Application/DependencyInjection.cs:45); when Engagement is switched off in a host it is DisabledBookmarkCountService (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/EngagementModule.cs:33); and when Engagement runs as its own process it is BookmarkCountServiceGrpcAdapter, swapped in with Replace by AddEngagementBookmarkCountClient() (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Contracts/DependencyInjection.cs:52, called from MMCA.ADC.Conference.Service/Program.cs:431). That is ADR-007 and ADR-008 made concrete: the C# call site never learns which one it got. The [ServiceContract] marker is what declares this intent in code rather than in a comment.
    • Walkthrough: two methods, both taking an explicit (non-defaulted) CancellationToken so every implementation, including the gRPC one, threads cancellation. GetBookmarkCountForSessionAsync(sessionId, cancellationToken) (IBookmarkCountService.cs:19) returns a bare int for one session. GetBookmarkCountsForSessionsAsync(sessionIds, cancellationToken) (IBookmarkCountService.cs:28-30) is the batched form, and its contract is spelled out in the doc comment (IBookmarkCountService.cs:22-23): every requested session id is present in the result, and a session with no bookmarks maps to 0. That sentence is a real contract, not decoration: it is what forces the disabled stub to project zeros rather than return an empty map. [Rubric §12, Performance & Scalability]: the batch method exists so the speaker dashboard resolves N sessions in one round trip instead of N, which matters most when the call is a network hop rather than a local query.
    • Why it's built this way: returning plain int / IReadOnlyDictionary rather than Result<T> keeps the contract trivially projectable onto a proto message; a fault surfaces as an exception (over gRPC, a status the caller's resilience pipeline can react to) instead of a failure payload each caller must unwrap. Living in .Shared is what keeps the reference direction legal: Conference references Engagement's contract assembly only, which the Conference service project spells out in a comment on its own ProjectReference (MMCA.ADC.Conference.Service/MMCA.ADC.Conference.Service.csproj:26).
    • Where it's used: Conference's GetSessionBookmarkCountHandler and the batched GetSessionBookmarkCountsHandler; on the producing side it is what BookmarkCountsGrpcService publishes over the wire.

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.UserSessionBookmarks · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/UserSessionBookmarks/DisabledBookmarkCountService.cs:7 · Level 1 · class (internal sealed)

    • What it is: the null-object implementation of IBookmarkCountService that a host registers when the Engagement module is switched off. Every count answers zero.
    • Depends on: IBookmarkCountService only.
    • Concept introduced, the disabled-module stub. [Rubric §2, Design Patterns] (Null Object) and [Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness] both apply. The module system lets a host boot a subset of modules; a module that is off must still satisfy the interfaces other modules resolve, or the container throws at startup and the whole host fails on a feature nobody asked for. So IModule exposes RegisterDisabledStubs, and Engagement's implementation registers this class plus the data-subject export stub (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/EngagementModule.cs:31-36). [Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity]: the degradation is graceful and legible, a session simply shows zero saves instead of erroring.
    • Walkthrough: GetBookmarkCountForSessionAsync returns Task.FromResult(0) with no query allocated at all (DisabledBookmarkCountService.cs:10-11). GetBookmarkCountsForSessionsAsync honours the batch contract the interface documents rather than returning an empty map: it projects the requested ids into a dictionary of zeros, (sessionIds ?? []).Distinct().ToDictionary(id => id, _ => 0) (DisabledBookmarkCountService.cs:21-22). Two guards are packed into that one line and the <remarks> above it explains the second (:14-17): ?? [] means a caller passing null still gets a usable empty result instead of a NullReferenceException, and Distinct() mirrors the real BookmarkCountService so a duplicate id collapses instead of throwing out of ToDictionary. Note there is no async here at all: both methods are synchronous returns wrapped in a completed task.

The comment in MMCA.ADC.Conference.Service/Program.cs:33-38 records the intended flow, and the pipeline comment at :326-332 states the ordering rule: the module registration runs first, then AddEngagementBookmarkCountClient() Replaces whatever is there with the gRPC adapter.
    • Where it's used: EngagementModule.RegisterDisabledStubs (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.API/EngagementModule.cs:33), called by ModuleLoader for a disabled module; it is the fallback the Conference service starts from before the gRPC client registration overwrites it.

Every collection defaults to [] and every nested row to new(), so an event with no roster serializes as empty reports.

    ISessionBookmarkUIService

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared.UserSessionBookmarks · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/UserSessionBookmarks/ISessionBookmarkUIService.cs:15 · Level 3 · interface

    • What it is: the narrow UI-side contract that lets the Conference session pages render a bookmark star and toggle it inline, without navigating to an Engagement page and without referencing the Engagement UI assembly.
    • Depends on: BookmarkWriteOutcome, Result and ErrorType from MMCA.Common.Shared.Abstractions (ISessionBookmarkUIService.cs:1), and the identifier aliases.
    • Concept introduced, the cross-module UI service contract. [Rubric §18, UI Architecture] assesses how one module's page composes another module's capability. The pattern here is optional resolution: Conference's pages hold the dependency as a nullable property and ask the container for it rather than injecting it, BookmarkService = ServiceProvider.GetService<ISessionBookmarkUIService>() (MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Public/Sessions/PublicSessionList.razor.cs:141, and, for the detail page, the same line inside the extracted SessionBookmarkButton toggle it renders, SessionBookmarkButton.razor.cs:56), so a host that never called AddEngagementUI() simply renders no stars instead of failing to construct the page. PublicSessionListView then takes it as a nullable [Parameter] (PublicSessionListView.razor.cs:71). [Rubric §7, Microservices Readiness]: this is the presentation-layer twin of what IBookmarkCountService does for the application layer.
    • Concept, Result all the way to the page. Every member reports its outcome as a Result carrying the API's own errors with their ErrorType intact, and the interface doc comment states the rule (ISessionBookmarkUIService.cs:9-13): the calling page branches instead of catching, and only the caller's own OperationCanceledException still propagates. [Rubric §9, API & Contract Design] and [Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]: a "not there" answer and a "the remove failed" answer are different facts, and a boolean cannot tell them apart. That is spelled out for the delete member (:28-29): a missing bookmark answers 404, which arrives as an ErrorType.NotFound failure.
    • Concept, one offline-aware write entry point. [Rubric §29, Resilience & Business Continuity] and [Rubric §19, State Management]: every bookmark write goes through SetBookmarkedAsync, which sends online when it can and otherwise puts the write on the device's offline write queue to be replayed on reconnect (ADR-144). The doc comment (ISessionBookmarkUIService.cs:37-55) fixes the rules a page can rely on: the newest intent wins and is always issued in full (any write still queued for the same user and session is dropped first); online, an add is sent with an Idempotency-Key and an add that meets "already bookmarked" counts as done; a device known to be offline queues at once without trying the network; an online call that fails with a transport fault is queued too, reusing the add's idempotency key so a request that reached the server is deduplicated on replay; any other failure is returned as it is; and a write the queue refuses (OfflineWrites.QueueFull, OfflineWrites.Unavailable) is returned as a failure, never as queued.
    • Walkthrough: three members, each shaped by a real UI need.
      • GetBookmarkedSessionIdsAsync(userId, cancellationToken) (ISessionBookmarkUIService.cs:20-21) returns Result<IReadOnlyDictionary<SessionIdentifierType, UserSessionBookmarkIdentifierType>>, a map rather than a set. A list page needs both facts at once: which sessions are starred, and the bookmark id it must send to un-star each one, so the dictionary saves a second round trip per row.
      • DeleteBookmarkAsync(bookmarkId, sessionId, cancellationToken) (:32-35) takes the session id even though the API key alone identifies the row. The doc comment says why (:24-26): the session-reminder layer (ADR-042 Wave 2) needs to know which session's scheduled local notification to cancel, and the bookmark id cannot answer that after the row is gone.
      • SetBookmarkedAsync(userId, sessionId, bookmarked, knownBookmarkId, cancellationToken) (:62-67) is the toggle. bookmarked is the state the user asked for; knownBookmarkId is the id the caller holds, when it holds one. It may be null for a star set by a queued add, in which case a remove resolves the id through the session-ids read, and a bookmark that is already gone counts as removed (:40-42). It returns a BookmarkWriteOutcome saying whether the write was confirmed or queued, with the new id after a confirmed add (:61).
    • Why it's built this way: the interface lives in .Shared, the assembly Conference already references, while its implementation lives in Engagement's UI project. That split is what makes the star a genuinely optional feature of the Conference page rather than a hard dependency. Routing every write through one toggle keeps the offline rules (coalescing, idempotency key reuse, duplicate-as-success) in one implementation, SessionBookmarkUIService (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:79-129), instead of in every page that draws a star. All three CancellationToken parameters are defaulted here, unlike on IBookmarkCountService, because the callers are Blazor event handlers rather than a generated gRPC client.
    • Where it's used: implemented by SessionBookmarkUIService (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Bookmarks/SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:36-41), registered scoped in DependencyInjection (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:35), consumed by Conference's PublicSessionList, PublicSessionDetail (through SessionBookmarkButton, whose toggle calls SetBookmarkedAsync at SessionBookmarkButton.razor.cs:122), PublicSessionListView (PublicSessionListView.razor.cs:164, :186) and PublicSessionBookmarkState (PublicSessionBookmarkState.cs:15). Its nullable-injection convention is cited as precedent by ISessionLiveUIService (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/SessionQuestions/ISessionLiveUIService.cs:4-5).

    • Concept, centralized route paths. [Rubric §25, Navigation & Information Architecture] assesses whether URL strings are declared once or scattered across NavigateTo call sites and @page directives. Every route here is either a const (parameterless) or a static method (id-carrying), so renaming a route touches one file and the compiler finds the call sites. [Rubric §27, Internationalization] shows up in an easy-to-miss detail: each interpolated route is built with string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, $"...") (EngagementRoutePaths.cs:12-14, :17-18, :35, :39-40) rather than plain interpolation, so a culture with non-ASCII digits or a different number format can never produce a URL the router will not match.
    • Walkthrough
      • Live layer (EngagementRoutePaths.cs:10-14): const string HappeningNow = "/happening-now", plus SessionDetails, SessionLive and SessionPresent, which build /conference/sessions/{id}, .../live and .../present.
      • Feedback (EngagementRoutePaths.cs:16-18): EventFeedback(eventId) and SessionFeedback(sessionId), whose outputs match the @page templates on the two feedback pages.
      • Badge check-in (EngagementRoutePaths.cs:20-23): MyBadge = "/my-badge", CheckInScan = "/check-in", OrganizerAttendance = "/organizer/attendance", the three routes carried by the pages later in this part.
      • Points (EngagementRoutePaths.cs:25-27): MyPoints = "/points" and OrganizerPointsOverview = "/organizer/points".
      • Tickets (EngagementRoutePaths.cs:29-35): OrganizerTickets = "/organizer/tickets" for the roster, and OrganizerTicketInsights = "/organizer/tickets/insights" with its builder OrganizerTicketInsightsFor(eventId), which appends ?eventId={id} because the insights page is reached from the roster carrying its selected event. The comment at :29-30 records why the attendee side adds no route: "Link my ticket" lives on the MyBadge page.
      • Self-service QR (EngagementRoutePaths.cs:39-40): SponsorVisit(sponsorId) and RoomCheckIn(roomId) build /engage/sponsors/{id} and /engage/rooms/{id}. The comment above them (EngagementRoutePaths.cs:37-38) records the design decision that matters to a reader: these are deep-link-only landings reached by scanning a printed code, so neither contributes a nav item.
    • Why it's built this way: methods are used wherever an id is embedded so the interpolation (and its invariant culture) lives in one place; plain consts are used for the parameterless routes because they must be usable in attribute and collection-initializer positions, which is exactly how EngagementUIModule consumes them.
    • Where it's used: seven of the constants seed the nav items in EngagementUIModule (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/EngagementUIModule.cs:33-42); the feedback and live builders are called from pages and services that link an attendee onward (SessionLive.razor.cs, SessionFeedback.razor.cs, SessionReminderPlanner.cs, LiveEventListener.razor.cs), TicketInsights uses the insights route, the host's AppActionRouteMap maps app actions onto these routes, and the QR builders are what a printed sponsor or room code encodes.

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/ScanOutcomeKind.cs:4 · Level 0 · enum (internal)

    • What it is: the four things one check-in attempt can mean to the organizer holding the phone, quoting the type's own summary (ScanOutcomeKind.cs:3). It lives in its own file beside CheckInScan, the page that produces and renders it.
    • Depends on: nothing.
    • Concept, the closed outcome vocabulary behind a UI feed. [Rubric §21, Accessibility] is the reason this is an enum and not a pre-formatted string: the page fans each member out through three separate switch expressions, one for the sentence (OutcomeText, CheckInScan.razor.cs:342-349), one for the alert severity (SeverityFor, :351-358) and one for the icon (IconFor, :360-367), so colour never carries the status alone. The markup pairs the severity with the icon on every row (CheckInScan.razor:114-117), which is what WCAG 2.1 AA asks for. [Rubric §27, i18n]: because the enum stays a symbol until render time, the wording lives entirely in the page's resource file.
    • Walkthrough: CheckedIn, AlreadyCheckedIn, NotABadge, Failed (ScanOutcomeKind.cs:6-9). AlreadyCheckedIn is not an error state: a repeat scan is a normal thing to happen at a door, so it maps to Severity.Warning with a replay icon (CheckInScan.razor.cs:354, :363) rather than to a failure. NotABadge covers a scanner reading a poster or sponsor QR and maps to Severity.Info (:355). Only Failed maps to Severity.Error (:356).
    • Why it's built this way: four named cases keep the render-time mapping exhaustive and reviewable in one screen. All three switch expressions still carry a _ => default arm (CheckInScan.razor.cs:348, :357, :366) so adding a member cannot throw at runtime, only produce the generic failure presentation until the arms are extended.

    CheckInState

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns.Rooms · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/Rooms/RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:197 · Level 0 · enum (protected, nested)

    • What it is: the eight states one scan of a printed room QR can put the page in, as seen by the attendee (RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:196). It is nested inside RoomCheckIn and is the single field its markup switches on.
    • Depends on: nothing (a bare enum). Its refusal values are produced by the page's mapping switch from the IsTransient flag and the CheckInErrorCodes value carried on SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>.
    • Concept introduced, the page-owned outcome enum. [Rubric §19, State Management] assesses whether a component's visible states are enumerated or reconstructed ad hoc from a scatter of booleans. This page has exactly one state field, so "confirm", "loading", "recorded", "nothing scheduled here", "code rejected", "event not published", "no answer yet, retry" and "unavailable" are mutually exclusive by construction, and the markup is a flat chain of comparisons (RoomCheckIn.razor:12, :16, :31, :67, :73, :81, :85, with the final else at :100) with no combination to reason about. [Rubric §9, API & Contract Design] is the other half of the story: the refusals cannot all be told apart by HTTP status, so the state is picked from the server's stable error code carried back on SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>, and its IsTransient flag (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/CheckIns/SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:20-25) separates "the server said no" from "no definitive answer arrived".
    • Walkthrough: eight members in the order the attendee meets them. Confirm (RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:200) is what an interactive arrival shows: the scanned room with a Check in button, and nothing posted yet (set at :91, rendered at RoomCheckIn.razor:16-30). Loading (RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:203) is the initial value of State (:56), so it covers the prerender, and it covers the in-flight post (:103). Recorded (:206) covers both a fresh check-in and a re-confirmed earlier one; the distinction is RoomCheckInResultDTO.AlreadyCheckedIn, not a separate state. NoCurrentSession (:209) means nothing is scheduled in that room right now, and, per the member comment, an unknown room reads the same way. NotPublished (:212) means the owning event is not published yet. CodeRejected (:215) means the scanned code is not the room's current one because the room's QR was re-issued; the markup points the attendee at the code on the door (RoomCheckIn.razor:73-80). Unavailable (RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:218) is the feature-off answer: per its member comment, the server answered and the answer is no. Transient (:221) is the absence of a definitive answer (rate limited, timed out, offline), the state the attendee can act on through the Retry button the markup renders beside it (RoomCheckIn.razor:92-98).
    • Why it's built this way: collapsing "unknown room" into NoCurrentSession and the feature gate into Unavailable is a deliberate disclosure choice: a printed code that produces a distinguishable answer for a room that does not exist would confirm which room ids do exist. Splitting Transient off Unavailable is the opposite move for the opposite reason: a timeout is not a refusal, so it must not read as "this code is not available", and the markup comment (RoomCheckIn.razor:87-88) records that the retry reuses the same attempt key, so a check-in whose first try did land reads as recorded rather than repeated. Confirm exists so that opening the link records nothing until its holder taps. See ADR-072 for the surrounding scan-surface decision.
    • Where it's used: only inside RoomCheckIn (RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:56, :91, :103, :123, :133-140, :151) and its markup. protected rather than private so the bUnit component tests can assert the rendered outcome (see RoomCheckInTests).
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the doc comment on the State property (RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:55) still says "six outcomes"; the enum itself has eight members.
