    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns.Sponsors · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/Sponsors/SponsorVisit.razor.cs:164 · Level 0 · enum (protected, nested)

    • What it is: the six states one scan of a printed sponsor-booth QR can put the page in. The sibling of CheckInState, nested inside SponsorVisit, with two fewer members because a sponsor booth has no "what is running here right now" question and its code carries no re-issuable room code.
    • Depends on: nothing (a bare enum); its refusal values are chosen from the IsTransient flag and the CheckInErrorCodes value on SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>.
    • Concept: the page-owned outcome enum is taught on CheckInState; the same reasoning applies unchanged here.
    • Walkthrough: Confirm (SponsorVisit.razor.cs:167), the booth shown with a Record visit button and nothing posted yet (set at :81, rendered at SponsorVisit.razor:17-31); Loading (SponsorVisit.razor.cs:170), the initial value of State (:51) and the in-flight state (:93); Recorded (:173), which covers both a first visit and a repeat, split in the markup by SponsorVisitResultDTO.AlreadyVisited (SponsorVisit.razor:34); NotPublished (SponsorVisit.razor.cs:176); Unavailable (:179); and Transient (:182), the no-definitive-answer state that renders a Retry button (SponsorVisit.razor:76-82). The mapping is a property-pattern switch over the outcome (SponsorVisit.razor.cs:119-124): IsTransient: true selects Transient, CheckInErrorCodes.EventNotPublished selects NotPublished, and everything else, including a null code, falls to Unavailable.
    • Why it's built this way: the member comment on Unavailable (SponsorVisit.razor.cs:178) folds "feature off" and "unknown sponsor" into one member, an answer the server gave, and the markup comment (SponsorVisit.razor:86-87) states the reason: the two are the same sentence to an attendee holding a phone, and naming them apart would only confirm which sponsor codes exist. That makes the collapse a [Rubric §26, Front-End Security] decision (no existence disclosure through error differentiation) as much as a copy decision. An unreachable service is deliberately not part of that collapse: it is Transient (SponsorVisit.razor.cs:181-182), because a timeout is no answer at all and the attendee can retry it.
    • Where it's used: only inside SponsorVisit (SponsorVisit.razor.cs:51, :81, :93, :109, :119-124, :135) and its markup; protected so SponsorVisitTests can drive it.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the enum's own summary (SponsorVisit.razor.cs:163) still says "five things"; it has six members, which the State property's comment (:50) does count as six.

    ScanOutcome

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/ScanOutcome.cs:4 · Level 1 · record (internal sealed)

    • What it is: one line in the organizer's on-screen scan feed: what happened to a badge, and to whom, in the order the organizer saw it (ScanOutcome.cs:3).
    • Depends on: ScanOutcomeKind.
    • Concept, the immutable UI event record. [Rubric §19, State Management] assesses where transient UI state lives and how it changes. The feed is a plain List<ScanOutcome> field on CheckInScan (CheckInScan.razor.cs:71) whose entries are never edited after creation: a new scan is inserted at index 0 and the list is trimmed from the tail (AddOutcome, CheckInScan.razor.cs:333-340, bounded by the const int MaxOutcomes = 10 at :24). Immutable entries plus a bounded list mean the feed cannot grow without limit during a long scanning session and cannot be retroactively rewritten by a later scan.
    • Walkthrough: a positional record with AttendeeName and Kind (ScanOutcome.cs:4). It is constructed in four places on the page, and the differences are the interesting part: new ScanOutcome(string.Empty, ScanOutcomeKind.NotABadge) when the scanned text is not a badge payload (CheckInScan.razor.cs:230), a named Failed when a manual write comes back a failure (:291), a Failed carrying whatever name the caller had when the response itself is a failure (:318), and the success path in RecordResultAsync, which resolves a name and picks AlreadyCheckedIn or CheckedIn from the response (:328-330). Where no name is available the page substitutes the localized Outcome.UnknownAttendee string (:329) rather than rendering an empty row.
    • Why it's built this way: keeping the name on the record (instead of re-resolving it at render time) means the feed is pure data by the time the markup runs, so re-rendering never triggers another lookup.
    • Where it's used: only inside CheckInScan; rendered as one MudAlert per entry (CheckInScan.razor:114-117).

    OrganizerEventPicker

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/OrganizerEventPicker.razor.cs:14 · Level 3 · class (partial)

    • What it is: the code-behind for a small event-chooser component shared by the organizer pages. It takes the published events and the currently selected one, tells its host when the organizer picks a different event, and offers the hosts one static loader that resolves the current event and the events to list.
    • Depends on: LiveEventContext (the event row it lists: a name and a live-window start), ILiveEventUIService and LiveEventLookup (the three-state current-event read, MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/SessionLive/LiveEventLookup.cs:10). Externals: Blazor [Parameter] / EventCallback<T> and the EventIdentifierType alias. The markup (the select control) is not in this file.
    • Walkthrough
      • Three parameters (OrganizerEventPicker.razor.cs:17-23): Events (IReadOnlyList<LiveEventContext>, default empty), SelectedEventId (EventIdentifierType?) and OnEventSelected (EventCallback<EventIdentifierType>). The host owns the selection; the picker only reports changes.
      • OffersAChoice(events) (:32-36) is a public static predicate returning events.Count > 1, after an ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull. It is static so the host pages can call it too, to drop their plain event-name heading while the picker (which already shows the chosen name) is on screen (doc comment :25-31).
      • LoadEventsAsync(liveEventService, cancellationToken) (:47-61) is the public static loader every host runs before it loads anything. It awaits GetCurrentEventAsync (:53) and returns that LiveEventLookup with an empty list when there is no current event (:54-57), so a host can tell a failed read (IsFailed, LiveEventLookup.cs:19) from no published event (LiveEventLookup.cs:22). Otherwise it reads GetPublishedEventsAsync and returns the published list, or the current event alone when that list is empty (OrganizerEventPicker.razor.cs:59-60). The doc comment (:38-46) states the rule: the current event stays the default, and a failed read of the published list degrades to the current event alone (no picker), never an error.
      • OrderedEvents (:63-65) sorts by LiveWindowStartUtc then by Name under StringComparer.CurrentCulture, so the list reads chronologically.
      • OnSelectedEventChangedAsync (:67-70) invokes OnEventSelected only when the chosen id is non-null and differs from SelectedEventId; re-selecting the current event returns Task.CompletedTask, which is why the callback is documented as never raised for the event already selected (:22).
    • Why it's built this way: a single event needs no chooser, so OffersAChoice keeps the single-event case unchanged for hosts. Keeping selection state in the host lets each page decide what a change reloads, and putting the load in one static method keeps the "failed read versus no event" distinction identical on every host.
    • Where it's used: hosted by CheckInScan (CheckInScan.razor:15, heading guard at :36, loader call at CheckInScan.razor.cs:87) and OrganizerAttendance (OrganizerAttendance.razor:15, guard at :36, loader call at OrganizerAttendance.razor.cs:74), and used by the ticket pages (TicketInsights and the Pages/Tickets/TicketRoster.razor.cs roster page); component-tested through CheckInScanTests and OrganizerAttendanceTests.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the select markup and its resource strings live outside this file.

    MyBadge

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/MyBadge.razor.cs:15 · Level 5 · class (partial)

    • What it is: the code-behind for the attendee's own badge page (@page "/my-badge", MyBadge.razor:1). It fetches the caller's opaque badge credential, encodes it as a QR code, and renders the attendee's name beside it as plain text.
    • Depends on: ICheckInUIService (MyBadge.razor.cs:17), BadgePayload (:66), and MyBadgeDTO as the value inside the fetch result. Externals: Blazor's [CascadingParameter] Task<AuthenticationState> (:19-20), MudBlazor's BreadcrumbItem/Icons, the shared QrCodeImage, PageLoadingState and DetailLoadStateContent components from MMCA.Common.UI.Components (the latter driven by DetailLoadState), and an injected IStringLocalizer<MyBadge> named L declared in the markup (MyBadge.razor:6).
    • Concept introduced, the opaque-credential badge. [Rubric §11, Security] and [Rubric §30, Compliance, Privacy & Data Governance] both apply, and the class summary states the rule (MyBadge.razor.cs:10-14): the QR carries only the credential, nothing about the person. Anyone photographing a badge across the room learns a GUID, not a name or an email, and the server remains the sole authority on which attendee that credential belongs to (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/CheckIns/Badges/BadgePayload.cs:6-11). The human-readable name is rendered beside the code as ordinary text (MyBadge.razor:42) so an organizer can confirm the badge belongs to the person holding it; it is never inside the code. [Rubric §21, Accessibility]: the QR image carries an AltText from the resource file, and its PixelsPerModule="14" plus Medium error correction are documented in the markup comment (MyBadge.razor:34-35) as making the code readable at arm's length and tolerant of glare or a fingerprint.
    • Concept, distinguishing "no badge" from "the fetch failed". [Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]: the page reads the result twice, once for the happy path and once for the shape of the failure. badgeResult.TryGetValue(out var badge) unwraps a success (:64); else if (!badgeResult.IsNotFound()) sets the error message only when the failure was something other than a 404 (:68-73), and the inline comment (:70-71) records that a not-found is simply an attendee who has no badge yet. The markup then has three distinct terminal states, not two: the failed-load body, a DetailLoadStateContent in its Failed state whose OnRetry is LoadAsync (MyBadge.razor:17-22), the empty-state alert when _payload is still null (:23-28), and the badge card (:29-49).
    • Walkthrough (teaching order)
      • State: a CancellationTokenSource field (MyBadge.razor.cs:22), the LifetimeToken property (:24-27, see below), the breadcrumb list (:29), a protected bool IsLoading that starts true (:32), and three privates for the error message, the encoded payload and the display name (:34-36).
      • LifetimeToken => _cts.LifetimeToken() (:27) is the token every await uses. The comment above it (:24-26) gives the reason: reading Token off a disposed source throws ObjectDisposedException, whereas Dispose cancels before it disposes, so a load that resumes after the attendee navigated away gets an already-cancelled token and exits through its OperationCanceledException path.
      • OnInitializedAsync (:38) is not async: it builds the two-item breadcrumb trail (:40-44) and returns LoadAsync() (:46).
      • LoadAsync (:50) is the load and, per its summary, also the Retry action (:49), which is why it begins by setting IsLoading = true and clearing _loadError (:52-53): a retry starts from the spinner, not from the previous error. Inside a try it awaits the cascaded AuthenticationState for state.User.Identity?.Name (:57-61) and calls CheckInService.GetMyBadgeAsync(LifetimeToken) (:63). Only on a successful unwrap does it compute _payload = BadgePayload.Format(badge.Credential) (:66).
      • Failure handling is the house pattern: OperationCanceledException is swallowed as expected during disposal (:75-78), and IsLoading is cleared in finally (:79-82) so the page can never be stuck on the spinner. Because the service returns a Result, an ordinary server refusal never reaches a catch at all.
      • Dispose(bool) / Dispose() (:87-107) are the standard disposable pattern with a _disposed guard, cancelling and disposing the token source so an in-flight fetch stops when the attendee navigates away.
    • Why it's built this way: encoding the payload on the client from a credential the server issued keeps the QR format in exactly one place, BadgePayload.Format (BadgePayload, MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/CheckIns/Badges/BadgePayload.cs:20), which is the same class the scanner side parses with (:30). Display and check-in cannot drift apart because they share the type and its mmca-adc:badge: prefix (:15).
    • Where it's used: routed at /my-badge behind a plain [Authorize] attribute (MyBadge.razor:2), so the route itself admits any signed-in attendee, while the nav item EngagementUIModule registers for it carries RequiredRole: RoleNames.Organizer (EngagementUIModule.cs:27), so only organizers see the link in the menu. Its QR is what CheckInScan reads at a session door.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the resource strings and the QrCodeImage rendering behaviour live outside this file; this section covers the code-behind and the small amount of markup cited.

    RoomCheckIn

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns.Rooms · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/Rooms/RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:24 · Level 5 · class (partial)

    • What it is: the code-behind for the room QR landing page (@page "/engage/rooms/{RoomId:int}", RoomCheckIn.razor:1). An attendee scans the code printed beside a room door, signs in if needed, lands here, sees the room, and taps Check in; the page then records the check-in. The scan never names a session: the server decides which session that room is hosting at this instant. The printed QR also carries the room's check-in code as ?code=, the proof of presence the server checks.
    • Depends on: ICheckInUIService (the post), SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult> (the return shape), RoomCheckInResultDTO (the payload), CheckInErrorCodes (the refusal vocabulary), IToastService (the snackbar), ViewerTimeZone (the viewer's clock, RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:37), and its own nested CheckInState. Externals: Blazor ComponentBase (RendererInfo, [Parameter], [SupplyParameterFromQuery]), MudBlazor BreadcrumbItem / MudAlert / MudButton / MudCard / Icons, and an injected IStringLocalizer<RoomCheckIn> named L supplied by the markup (RoomCheckIn.razor:5).
    • Concept introduced, the confirm-to-write landing page. [Rubric §18, UI Architecture] assesses component/behavior separation and render-mode discipline. Arriving from a scan is half the interaction; one tap is the other half. The page prepares the write in OnParametersSetAsync and posts it only from ConfirmAsync, the Check in button's handler (RoomCheckIn.razor:24-25). That makes the Blazor render-mode question load-bearing in a narrower way: a prerendered pass and the interactive pass both run the lifecycle, so the guard at RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:75-76 (!RendererInfo.IsInteractive || RoomId == _postedRoomId && CheckInCode == _postedCheckInCode, compared ordinally) keeps one scan to one prepared attempt, while a scan of a different room, or of the same room with a different code, reusing the routed instance prepares a new one. The class comment (just above :24) gives the reason for the tap: a link opened from anywhere (a forwarded message, an app link the phone resolved on its own) records nothing until its holder confirms. [Rubric §19, State Management] covers the single-field state model taught on CheckInState.
    • Concept introduced, the retryable write under one attempt key. A phone at a crowded door loses packets, so a post that got no answer must be retryable without risking a double record. Each scan gets one Idempotency-Key, minted as Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N") when the scan changes (RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:87) and kept in _attemptKey (:53) for every retry of that scan, the Retry button included. The comment (:84-86) gives the reason: a retry whose first try did land replays that first answer instead of reading as a repeat check-in. The server half is the IdempotentAttribute on the room-visits endpoint (CheckInsController.cs:194). [Rubric §11, Security] applies through @attribute [Authorize] (RoomCheckIn.razor:2): the page identifies the attendee from the authenticated session, so a scanned code carries no identity of its own, and the ?code= value proves presence at the door rather than who is scanning.
    • Walkthrough (teaching order)
      • [Parameter] RoomIdentifierType RoomId (RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:27) is bound from the {RoomId:int} route constraint, so an unparseable code never reaches the component. [SupplyParameterFromQuery(Name = "code")] string? CheckInCode (:33) reads the room's check-in code from the query string; per its doc comment (:29-32) it is absent on a QR printed before the room had a code, which the server accepts until an organizer issues one. The injected ICheckInUIService, IToastService and ViewerTimeZone follow (:35-37), then a CancellationTokenSource (:39), the LifetimeToken property (:44), the breadcrumb list (:46), the _postedRoomId and _postedCheckInCode pair holding the scan this instance last showed, posted or is posting (:48-50), and the _attemptKey string (:53) holding the current scan's idempotency key.
      • LifetimeToken => _cts.LifetimeToken() (:44) is the token every await on the page uses. The comment above it (:41-43) records why: reading Token off a disposed source throws ObjectDisposedException, while Dispose cancels before it disposes, so a post that resumes after the attendee navigated away sees an already-cancelled token and exits through its OperationCanceledException path.
      • State (:56) starts at CheckInState.Loading and is protected with a private setter; Result (:59) holds the RoomCheckInResultDTO and is documented as present only in the Recorded state.
      • OnInitialized (:61-66) is a synchronous expression-bodied method that builds the two-item breadcrumb trail, so even the non-interactive prerender has a complete chrome. OnParametersSetAsync (:68) is not async: it returns Task.CompletedTask if the render is not interactive or the room and code match the last scan (:75-79). Otherwise it records the scan (:81-82), mints a fresh _attemptKey (:87), clears Result and moves to CheckInState.Confirm (:89-91), posting nothing. The comment (:70-74) gives the reason the code is part of the guard: rescanning the room's current door code while an out-of-date one is refused on screen changes only ?code, and must be a new attempt (M247, the SessionLive per-id pattern).
      • ConfirmAsync (:96) is the Check in button's handler and RetryAsync (:99) is the Retry button's (RoomCheckIn.razor:95); both send RecordCheckInAsync for _postedRoomId under the current key and do nothing when no scan has been shown.
      • RecordCheckInAsync (RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:101) resets State to Loading and clears Result (:103-104), copies _attemptKey into a local attemptKey that identifies the scan this post belongs to (:106-108), then awaits CheckInService.RecordRoomCheckInAsync(roomId, _postedCheckInCode, attemptKey, LifetimeToken) (:112).
      • Right after the await, a stale-scan check (:115-118) returns when attemptKey no longer equals _attemptKey: a newer scan took over the page while this one was in flight, and its own post owns the state.
      • The success branch (:120-131) assigns Result, moves to CheckInState.Recorded, and raises a success toast only when Result?.AlreadyCheckedIn == false (:125-128): a rescan is a normal thing to do, so it renders as information (RoomCheckIn.razor:33-47) rather than as a second celebration.
      • The refusal branch (RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:133-140) is a property-pattern switch over the outcome: IsTransient: true becomes Transient (checked first, so a timeout never reads as a refusal), ErrorCode: CheckInErrorCodes.NoCurrentSession becomes NoCurrentSession, ErrorCode: CheckInErrorCodes.EventNotPublished becomes NotPublished, ErrorCode: CheckInErrorCodes.RoomCodeRejected becomes CodeRejected (:138), and everything else (including a null code) falls through the discard arm to Unavailable. This is the client-side consumer of the contract that SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult> exists to carry.
      • catch (OperationCanceledException) when (LifetimeToken.IsCancellationRequested) (:142-145) is silent only when the page's own token was cancelled, that is when the attendee navigated away; any other exception, including a cancellation the page did not ask for such as a client timeout, lands on Transient only when the attempt key is still current (:147-152), so a stale scan's failure cannot overwrite a newer scan's state. The CA1031 suppression around that catch (:146, :148) carries the reason inline: a fault with no definitive answer is the retryable state, never "not available".
      • OnAfterRenderAsync (:160-166) runs on the first render only: it awaits ViewerTime.EnsureResolvedAsync(LifetimeToken) and calls StateHasChanged() when the zone changed, so the recorded time moves from the UTC fallback to the viewer's clock once JS interop is available (doc comment :155-159).
      • FormatCheckedInOn (:176-177) is an instance method that renders the recorded instant through ViewerTime.Format(checkedInOn.UtcDateTime). The XML comment (:168-175) gives the reason: the attendee is comparing the timestamp against the clock on the wall beside them, and DateTimeOffset.ToLocalTime would read the server's clock on Blazor Server and during prerender. [Rubric §27, Internationalization] covers both halves of that, the viewer-zone formatting and the fact that every visible string is an L["..."] resource lookup (ADR-027).
      • PointsLine (:186-194) picks the line under a first check-in from the RoomCheckInResultDTO: PointsPaused gives the PointsPaused string (session points are switched off, nothing is awarded), otherwise EarnsPoints selects Success.PointsHint ("added to your total") or NoPointsThisTimeSlot for a second check-in in the same time slot (doc comment :179-185).
      • Dispose(bool) / Dispose() (:224-246) implement the standard disposable pattern with a _disposed latch, cancelling and disposing _cts so an in-flight post stops when the attendee navigates away.
    • Why it's built this way: the class comment (just above RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:24) states the constraints. The write runs on the interactive render only, once per scan rather than once per page instance, and only after the attendee confirms: a prerender must not spend a round trip, a back button must not read as a second arrival, and a link that reached a phone some other way must not record anything on its own. The server is idempotent per session regardless (a repeat returns AlreadyCheckedIn), so the per-scan guard is about not making a pointless call rather than about correctness; the attempt key adds the same guarantee for a retry, which the endpoint replays rather than re-executes. Resolving the session server-side from the room, instead of encoding it in the QR, means the printed code does not change when the schedule moves (ADR-072); only re-issuing the room's check-in code retires an old print, which is what CodeRejected reports. The page complements organizer badge scanning at the door rather than replacing it: one session yields one check-in by either path, which is exactly what the "already checked in" branch says (RoomCheckIn.razor:35-36).
    • Where it's used: the target of the room QR rendered on the Conference room detail page (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Rooms/RoomDetail.razor:64, a QrCodeButton over ConferenceRoutePaths.RoomCheckInLink(id, checkInCode), ConferenceRoutePaths.cs:68) per ADR-071. The post lands on CheckInsController's room-visits endpoint (CheckInsController.cs:193, [Idempotent] at :194, feature-gated on EngagementFeatures.RoomCheckIn at :195) and is handled by RecordRoomCheckInHandler. [Rubric §28, Front-End Testing]: covered by RoomCheckInTests (bUnit), and the architecture suite carries a RoomCheckInModeTests contract test. Render-mode background: ADR-056.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the confirm card, the outcome copy, the success card, the points hint and the Retry button live in RoomCheckIn.razor (:16-30, :31-66, :85-99) and the resource files, not in this code-behind. Whether a given deployment has EngagementFeatures.RoomCheckIn on is configuration, not source.

    SponsorVisit

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns.Sponsors · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/Sponsors/SponsorVisit.razor.cs:26 · Level 5 · class (partial)

    • What it is: the code-behind for the sponsor-booth QR landing page (@page "/engage/sponsors/{SponsorId:int}", SponsorVisit.razor:1). The attendee scans the booth's printed code with the phone camera, signs in if needed, lands here, and taps Record visit; the page then records the visit.
    • Depends on: ICheckInUIService, SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>, SponsorVisitResultDTO, CheckInErrorCodes, IToastService, ViewerTimeZone (SponsorVisit.razor.cs:33), its nested VisitState, and (from the markup) ConferenceRoutePaths for the follow-on "all sponsors" link. Externals as on RoomCheckIn: Blazor RendererInfo / [Parameter], MudBlazor components, and an injected IStringLocalizer<SponsorVisit> (SponsorVisit.razor:6).
    • Concept: the confirm-to-write landing page is taught on RoomCheckIn; this page is the same shape with no room code and a simpler refusal map. The one difference worth naming is what happens after success: [Rubric §25, Navigation & Information Architecture] assesses whether a dead-end page gives the reader somewhere to go, and this one ends with a filled "all sponsors" button back into the public sponsor list (SponsorVisit.razor:57-63), which the room page has no equivalent of because a room scan is followed by sitting down.
    • Walkthrough of what differs from RoomCheckIn
      • [Parameter] SponsorIdentifierType SponsorId (SponsorVisit.razor.cs:29) instead of a room id, and no query-string code; LifetimeToken (:40, the same disposed-source guard as on RoomCheckIn, explained in the comment above it) backs every await; _postedSponsorId (:45) is a nullable SponsorIdentifierType holding the sponsor this instance last posted (or is posting); _attemptKey (:48) is the current booth's idempotency key; State defaults to VisitState.Loading (:51) and Visit holds a SponsorVisitResultDTO (:54).
      • OnInitialized (:56-61) only builds the breadcrumbs; OnParametersSetAsync (:63) carries an inline comment naming the pattern it follows (:65-66): the visit is a write, so it stays off the prerender pass, and the interactive instance is the one that owns the round trip (the ADCHome pattern). The guard is !RendererInfo.IsInteractive || SponsorId == _postedSponsorId (:67), so a deep link to another booth reusing the routed instance (M247, the SessionLive per-id pattern) prepares a new attempt. Past the guard it records the sponsor (:72), mints one attempt key per scanned booth (:77, comment :74-76 citing A-27), clears Visit and moves to VisitState.Confirm (:79-81), posting nothing.
      • ConfirmAsync (:86) backs the Record visit button (SponsorVisit.razor:25-26) and RetryAsync (SponsorVisit.razor.cs:89) backs the Retry button (SponsorVisit.razor:79); both send RecordVisitAsync for _postedSponsorId under the same key, exactly as on the room page.
      • RecordVisitAsync (SponsorVisit.razor.cs:91) resets State to Loading and clears Visit (:93-94) before calling CheckInService.RecordSponsorVisitAsync(sponsorId, _attemptKey, LifetimeToken) (:98).
      • A stale-scan check (:101-104) returns when sponsorId != _postedSponsorId, because a newer scan took over the page while this one was in flight. Unlike the room page, the check compares sponsor ids rather than attempt keys, since a booth scan has no code that can change on its own.
      • Success (:106-117) sets Visit, moves to VisitState.Recorded, and toasts only on a first visit (Visit?.AlreadyVisited == false, :111-114).
      • The refusal map (:119-124) is a property-pattern switch with fewer arms than the room page's: IsTransient: true selects Transient, only CheckInErrorCodes.EventNotPublished is distinguished among the refusals, and everything else is Unavailable. There is no room-style "nothing scheduled here" or "code rejected" case, because a booth is not on a schedule and its QR carries no code.
      • catch (OperationCanceledException) when (LifetimeToken.IsCancellationRequested) (:126-129) stays silent only when the attendee navigated away; catch (Exception) when (sponsorId == _postedSponsorId) (:131-136, inside the same inline CA1031 suppression as the room page) maps any other fault to Transient, only for the current scan.
      • OnAfterRenderAsync (:144-150) resolves the viewer's time zone on first render and calls StateHasChanged() if it changed, exactly as on the room page.
      • FormatVisitedOn (:160-161) is an instance method over ViewerTime.Format(visitedOn.UtcDateTime), identical in mechanism to the room page's, with the reason in its XML comment (:152-159): the attendee is at the booth, and ToLocalTime would be the server's clock on Blazor Server and during prerender.
      • Dispose(bool) / Dispose() (:185-207) are the same disposable pattern over _cts.
    • Why it's built this way: the class comment (just above SponsorVisit.razor.cs:26) says the write runs on the interactive render only and once per scanned sponsor, and that the server is idempotent per sponsor regardless of the guard, so the per-sponsor guard is about not making a pointless round trip rather than about correctness; a retry under the same attempt key is replayed by the endpoint's [Idempotent] attribute (CheckInsController.cs:159) rather than re-executed. The single confirm tap (SponsorVisit.razor:19) keeps a link opened outside a booth from recording a visit on its own while costing an attendee at the booth one tap; ADR-072 records the attendee-self-recorded scan surfaces this page belongs to.
    • Where it's used: the target of the sponsor QR rendered on the Conference sponsor detail page (MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Conference/MMCA.ADC.Conference.UI/Pages/Sponsors/SponsorDetail.razor:73, a QrCodeButton over ConferenceRoutePaths.SponsorVisitLink, ConferenceRoutePaths.cs:65). The post lands on CheckInsController's sponsor-visits endpoint (CheckInsController.cs:158, feature-gated on EngagementFeatures.SponsorVisits at CheckInsController.cs:160, see EngagementFeatures and ADR-031) and is handled by RecordSponsorVisitHandler. Component-tested by SponsorVisitTests.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: the confirm card, the success card, the points hint, the "already visited" copy and the Retry button live in SponsorVisit.razor (:17-31, :32-64, :69-83) and its resources. How many points a visit earns is decided server-side by the points earn rules, not here.

    AttendeeSearchPanel

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/AttendeeSearchPanel.razor.cs:16 · Level 7 · class (partial, DataGridListPageBase<AttendeeSummary>)

    • What it is: the manual check-in fallback, a paged, sortable, mobile-aware search over the Identity users endpoint with a per-row check-in action. It is a component, not a page: it has no @page directive and is embedded by CheckInScan.
    • Depends on: DataGridListPageBase<TDto> as its base (AttendeeSearchPanel.razor.cs:16), IAttendeeLookupService plus AttendeeSummary and AttendeeSearchField (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/Lookups/IAttendeeLookupService.cs:15, :39), MobileInfiniteScrollList<TItem>, and Result for the mobile fetch signature (:3, :79). Externals: MudBlazor MudDataGrid/GridState/GridData, and an injected IStringLocalizer<AttendeeSearchPanel> (AttendeeSearchPanel.razor:5).
    • Concept introduced, extracting a list surface out of a page. [Rubric §15, Best Practices & Code Quality] and [Rubric §18, UI Architecture]: the class summary records the reason for the split (AttendeeSearchPanel.razor.cs:10-15), namely that the page owns the scan loop and its own cancellation while the grid keeps the shared base's behaviour (server paging, mobile card layout, state restore) unchanged. Inheriting the framework base rather than hand-rolling a grid is what buys the mobile path: [Rubric §22, Responsive & Cross-Browser] shows in ReloadActiveLayoutAsync (:59-60), which delegates to the base's protected ReloadActiveLayoutAsync(_infiniteList) (MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Pages/Common/DataGridListPageBase.cs:1746-1755): on a phone with a card list it saves the filter state and resets the list from page 1, otherwise it reloads the grid, so the same filter change reloads whichever layout is live.
    • Walkthrough
      • Contract with the base: Title from the localizer (:19) and GridRef => _dataGrid (:32), which is how the base drives ReloadServerData(); OnMobileDataRequestedAsync (:55) routes the base's mobile hook back through the same reload, and RetryLoadAsync (:57) is what the empty-state retry button calls.
      • Parameters from the host page: CanCheckIn (:24) gates the per-row action, and OnCheckIn (:27) is the EventCallback<AttendeeSummary> raised by CheckInAsync (:127). The component performs no write of its own; it reports which row was actioned and lets the page decide.
      • Filter persistence: SaveFilters / RestoreFilters (:39-52) round-trip the search term and the chosen field through the base's state store, with Enum.TryParse falling back to LastName if the stored value is unreadable (:49-51).
      • Search handling: OnSearchChangedAsync and OnSearchFieldChangedAsync (:62-72) each set a field and return ReloadActiveLayoutAsync() directly (they are plain Task-returning methods, not async). The markup wires the text field with Immediate="true" DebounceInterval="300" (AttendeeSearchPanel.razor:12), so typing does not fire a request per keystroke, a [Rubric §23, Front-End Performance] detail.
      • Data loading: LoadServerData (:74-77) is LoadServerDataAsync(state, SearchAsync, ApplySearchTerm), handing the base the private SearchAsync (:96-103) as its fetch delegate. SearchAsync passes the filter bag to AttendeeLookup.SearchAsync(filters, page, pageSize, sortColumn, sortDirection, cancellationToken) verbatim (doc comment :90-95): the grid's column operators on LastName, FirstName and Email, and the search box's entry under the field's own key or under the ~search alias the base class moves it to when that column is also filtered, so both apply. FetchMobilePageAsync (:79-88) builds a filter bag, applies the search term, calls SearchAsync with "LastName" / "asc" (:87) and returns Task<Result<(IReadOnlyList<AttendeeSummary> Items, int TotalItems)>>, pinning the sort since the card layout has no sort UI. The markup binds it through FetchPageResult (AttendeeSearchPanel.razor:30), the Result-aware overload, which is what lets a failed page render ListNoRecordsContent with LoadFailed and a retry rather than an empty list (:86).
      • ApplySearchTerm (:109-125) is the load-bearing piece and its doc comment explains it (:105-108, echoed in the markup at :15): the Identity users endpoint ANDs its filters, so one search box broadcast across email, first name and last name would match nobody. The single term is therefore applied to exactly the field the organizer picked, as a "contains" filter (:116-124).
    • Why it's built this way: an organizer at a door needs the fallback to be fast and forgiving, and the shared base already solved paging, mobile layout and state restore for every other list in the app. Raising an EventCallback instead of calling the check-in service directly keeps the write path (and its scope, target and error reporting) in one place, the page. [Rubric §21, Accessibility]: both action buttons carry a per-row aria-label built from the attendee's display name (AttendeeSearchPanel.razor:43, :79), so a screen-reader user hears which person a "Check in" button belongs to.
    • Where it's used: rendered unconditionally near the bottom of the scan page, <AttendeeSearchPanel CanCheckIn="CanCheckIn" OnCheckIn="ManualCheckInAsync" /> (CheckInScan.razor:127). The comment above it (CheckInScan.razor:122-123) states the intent: on web and Windows heads there is no camera, so this search is the check-in surface.

    CheckInScan

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Pages.CheckIns · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Pages/CheckIns/CheckInScan.razor.cs:21 · Level 10 · class (partial)

    • What it is: the organizer check-in surface (@page "/check-in", [Authorize(Roles = RoleNames.Organizer)], CheckInScan.razor:1-2). On a head with a camera it loops the shared barcode scanner and posts each badge payload; everywhere else the manual search below the scan area is the whole page. Both paths write through the same endpoints and report the attendee by name.
    • Depends on: ICheckInUIService, IAttendeeLookupService, ISessionLookupService, ILiveEventUIService, IBarcodeScannerService and IToastService (CheckInScan.razor.cs:26-31); the shared contracts BadgePayload, CheckInScope, CheckInAttendeeRequest, ManualCheckInRequest, CheckInResultDTO; LiveEventContext and SessionInfo; Result and ErrorType (:4); ScanOutcome / ScanOutcomeKind for the feed; and the AttendeeSearchPanel and OrganizerEventPicker components.
    • Concept introduced, the capability-gated scan loop. [Rubric §18, UI Architecture] and the device-capability abstraction of ADR-042 meet here. ScannerAvailable => Scanner.IsSupported (:46, with the ADR named in the comment at :45) is the whole capability switch: the markup renders the scan card only when it is true (CheckInScan.razor:78), and every head that cannot open a camera falls through to the manual panel with no conditional compilation and no per-platform page. Camera permission is asked once, before the loop: Scanner.EnsureCameraAccessAsync (CheckInScan.razor.cs:210) returning false toasts a Snackbar.CameraDenied warning and returns (:210-214), so a denial leaves the organizer on the page with the reason and the manual search rather than on a camera surface that stays black (comment :208-209). [Rubric §11, Security]: scanned text is untrusted input, so BadgePayload.TryExtractCredential screens it before any request goes out (:228), and a poster or sponsor QR is reported as a skipped scan rather than an error (comment :224-227). [Rubric §24, Forms, Validation & UX Safety]: CanCheckIn (:49-50) refuses to start a scan or a manual write until a target exists, and the markup renders an inline "pick a target" alert when it is false (CheckInScan.razor:69-73).
    • Walkthrough (teaching order)
      • Constants and state: MaxOutcomes = 10 bounds the on-screen feed (CheckInScan.razor.cs:24); the CancellationTokenSource (:33), LifetimeToken (:38), IsLoading (:43), _loadError, _liveEvent, the _events list of published events that feeds the OrganizerEventPicker (:54), _sessions and _selectedSessionId (:52-56), the _loadGeneration counter (:63, explained below), the scope field (:68), the _isScanning flag and the _outcomes list (:70-71).
      • LifetimeToken => _cts.LifetimeToken() (:38) is the token every await on the page uses (catalog load, the camera-access check, Scanner.ScanAsync, both writes, the name lookup). The comment above it (:35-37) explains that reading Token off a disposed source throws ObjectDisposedException; because Dispose cancels before it disposes, a handler resuming after navigation gets a cancelled token and stops through its OperationCanceledException path.
      • Default scope: _scope = CheckInScope.Session with a comment that is real operational knowledge (:65-68, repeated for the reader in the markup at CheckInScan.razor:43-45), namely that the conference runs door and arrival check-in through TicketLeap, so session check-in is the working path and Event scope is kept for future info-desk use.
      • OnInitializedAsync (CheckInScan.razor.cs:73) is not async: it builds the breadcrumbs and returns RunLoadAsync(LoadEventAsync) (:81).
      • LoadEventAsync (:85-101) calls OrganizerEventPicker.LoadEventsAsync(LiveEventService, LifetimeToken) (:87). A failed read sets the localized load error and returns (:88-93), so an outage shows the failed-load body with Retry rather than reading as "no published event". Otherwise it stores the current event and the picker's events (:95-96) and, when there is a current event, awaits LoadSessionsAsync(_liveEvent.EventId) (:97-100).
      • Event switching: OnEventSelectedAsync (:107) is the handler the picker's OnEventSelected callback targets (CheckInScan.razor:15). It ignores an id not in _events (CheckInScan.razor.cs:109-113), calls StopScanning() and sets _liveEvent to the chosen event (:115-116), and returns ReloadSessionsAsync(eventId) (:117).
      • RetryLoadAsync (:124-125) is the OnRetry target of the failed-load body (CheckInScan.razor:25): it reloads the selected event's sessions, or runs LoadEventAsync again when no event was resolved because the event read failed (doc comment CheckInScan.razor.cs:120-123). ReloadSessionsAsync (:128-133) clears the session choice and session list (sessions belong to one event) and returns RunLoadAsync(() => LoadSessionsAsync(eventId)).
      • RunLoadAsync(Func<Task> load) (:136-159) is the one loading wrapper. It bumps _loadGeneration first, so anything in flight now belongs to an older generation (:138-140), clears _loadError and sets IsLoading (:141-142), awaits the load (:146), swallows a disposal-time OperationCanceledException (:148-151), and in finally clears IsLoading only when the generation is unchanged (:152-158), so a superseded load cannot hide the spinner of a newer selection.
      • LoadSessionsAsync (:162-182) is the shared session loader. It snapshots the generation, awaits the Result-returning catalog lookup (:166), and drops the result if the generation moved while it was in flight (:167-170), so a slow earlier load never overwrites a newer selection's list. A failed result sets the load error (:172-176); otherwise it filters sessions to the given event id, ordering by start time with ?? DateTime.MaxValue so unscheduled sessions sort last, then by title under StringComparer.CurrentCulture (:178-181).
      • Target selection: OnScopeChangedAsync stops any running scan when the scope changes (:184-189), which prevents a scan started against one target from continuing under another; OnSessionChanged just records the selection (:191).
      • StartScanningAsync (:198-249) is the loop. It refuses to start twice or without a target (:200-203), runs the camera-access check described above (:210-214), then repeatedly awaits Scanner.ScanAsync(LifetimeToken) while _isScanning holds and cancellation has not been requested (:216-218). A null payload means cancelled, and the loop ends quietly (:219-222, doc comment :193-197). A non-badge payload adds a NotABadge outcome, calls StateHasChanged() immediately, and continues (:228-233): the repaint is deliberate, because the next ScanAsync waits on the camera and the operator must see why that code was skipped in the meantime (comment :224-227). Otherwise it submits and calls StateHasChanged() so the feed paints between scans (:235-237), with a BL0012 suppression whose inline reason says the same thing (:236).
      • SubmitScanAsync (:253-267) builds a CheckInAttendeeRequest carrying the credential, the scope, the event id and, only in session scope, the selected session (:255-261). It does not catch anything: the write (CheckInByCredentialAsync(request, LifetimeToken), :265) returns a Result that RecordResultAsync turns into a Failed row while the loop keeps scanning, and a genuine cancellation propagates to the loop's own handler (:263-266).
      • ManualCheckInAsync (:270-308) is the fallback the panel raises. It toasts a warning when no target is selected (:272-276), builds a ManualCheckInRequest by user id (:280-286), and on a failed result adds a named Failed outcome (:291) plus a toast whose wording depends on why it failed: a refusal the API stated is shown verbatim through result.LocalizedErrorMessage(L), while an ErrorType.Unexpected fault keeps the page's own wording instead of raw diagnostic text (:293-298). [Rubric §11, Security] and [Rubric §13, Observability & Operability]: that branch is the boundary between what an organizer may read and what belongs in the logs.
      • RecordResultAsync (:314-331) turns one response into an outcome. A failed Result becomes a Failed row (:316-320). The scan path has no name to start from because a badge carries only a credential, so it resolves one via AttendeeLookup.GetDisplayNameAsync(checkIn.UserId, LifetimeToken) (:322-326); the manual path already has one and skips the lookup. Finally the response's AlreadyCheckedIn flag selects the outcome kind (:330), which is how a repeat scan reads as a recognisable warning instead of an error.
      • Presentation helpers OutcomeText / SeverityFor / IconFor (:342-367) and the bounded AddOutcome (:333-340), covered under ScanOutcomeKind.
      • Dispose(bool) (:371-386) clears _isScanning before cancelling and disposing the token source (:380-382), so the loop's condition fails on the next iteration as well as its await being cancelled.
    • Why it's built this way: one page serving both a camera head and a keyboard head is a deliberate choice, and it is only affordable because the scan capability is behind an injected interface. Treating a duplicate as a first-class outcome rather than an error is the other design decision that matters at a real door: the organizer needs to see who the badge belongs to either way, which is why CheckInResultDTO carries AlreadyCheckedIn instead of returning a conflict (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.Shared/CheckIns/CheckInResultDTO.cs:3-7, :14).
    • Where it's used: routed at /check-in, Organizer-only, and surfaced in the nav by EngagementUIModule with the same role requirement (EngagementUIModule.cs:39). It writes through CheckInService to the CheckInsController endpoints. Component-tested by CheckInScanTests and CheckInScanOutcomeTests.
    • Caveats / not-in-source: what the camera actually does on each platform is behind IBarcodeScannerService (EnsureCameraAccessAsync at MMCA.Common/Source/Presentation/MMCA.Common.UI/Services/Capabilities/Media/IBarcodeScannerService.cs:22) and is covered in the device-capability chapter, not here.

      • LoadEventAsync (:64-103) is both the initial load and the Retry action while no event has been resolved (doc comment :60-63). It bumps _loadGeneration (:66-68), clears the error and sets IsLoading (:69-70), then calls OrganizerEventPicker.LoadEventsAsync(LiveEventService, LifetimeToken) (:74). A failed read sets the localized load error and returns (:75-80), so an outage is not shown as "no published event"; no current event returns quietly (:82-85); otherwise it stores the selected id, name and picker events (:87-89) and awaits LoadStatsAsync(liveEvent.EventId) (:90). It swallows a disposal-time cancellation (:92-95), and the finally clears IsLoading only when the generation is unchanged (:96-102).
      • OnEventSelectedAsync (:106) is the picker callback target (OrganizerAttendance.razor:15). It ignores an id not in _events (OrganizerAttendance.razor.cs:108-112), swaps in the selected id and name (:114-115), and returns ReloadStatsAsync(eventId) (:116).
      • RetryLoadAsync (:123-124) is the OnRetry target of the failed-load body (OrganizerAttendance.razor:25): it reloads the selected event's figures, or runs LoadEventAsync again when the event read itself failed (doc comment OrganizerAttendance.razor.cs:119-122).
      • ReloadStatsAsync (:127-153) bumps _loadGeneration first, so anything in flight now belongs to an older generation (:129-131), clears _stats, _rows and the error and sets IsLoading (:133-136), then awaits LoadStatsAsync under the same swallow-cancel and generation-gated finally as the initial load (:138-152).
      • LoadStatsAsync (:156-187) is the shared loader: it fetches the rollup with GetAttendanceStatsAsync(eventId, LifetimeToken) (:160), drops the result if a newer selection superseded it (:161-164), sets the localized load error and returns on a failed Result (:166-170), builds the rows (:172), re-checks the generation (:173-176), stores _stats (:178), and if the row build returned null clears the rows and raises the load error (:179-184), otherwise assigns _rows (:186).
      • BuildSessionRowsAsync (:194) returns Task<List<SessionAttendanceRow>?> instead of assigning state itself: it short-circuits to an empty list when the rollup has no session rows, avoiding a pointless catalog fetch (:196-199). The catalog fetch itself uses SessionLookup.GetAllAsync(LifetimeToken) (:201). A failed catalog fetch returns null (:202-205), which LoadStatsAsync turns into cleared rows plus the same load error rather than silently rendering untitled rows. Otherwise it projects each DTO into a SessionAttendanceRow, substituting the localized Sessions.DeletedTitle when the catalog does not know the session (:210-215). The comment (:207-209) gives the reasoning: the catalog holds every live session of every edition, so a checked-in session missing from it was deleted after the check-ins were recorded, and its row is kept because the attendance happened. Sorting is OrderByDescending(Count) then ThenBy(Title, StringComparer.CurrentCulture) (:216-217), a culture-aware tie-break, so the busiest sessions lead.
      • Dispose (:220-242) is the same disposable pattern as the other check-in pages.
    • Why it's built this way: sorting and labelling once, on load, keeps the markup a pure loop over _rows (OrganizerAttendance.razor:68) with no I/O in the render path. [Rubric §21, Accessibility]: that markup is a real MudSimpleTable with a <caption>, <th scope="col"> headers and a <th scope="row"> per session (OrganizerAttendance.razor:59-76), not a styled div grid, so a screen reader announces the counts with their session names. [Rubric §27, i18n]: both the headline figure and each row count are formatted ToString("N0", CultureInfo.CurrentCulture) (:44, :72).
    • Where it's used: routed at /organizer/attendance and surfaced as an Organizer-only nav item by EngagementUIModule (EngagementUIModule.cs:40). Its numbers come from the same check-in rows that CheckInScan writes. Component-tested by OrganizerAttendanceTests.

    EngagementUIModule

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/EngagementUIModule.cs:22 · Level 11 · class (sealed)

    • What it is: the Engagement module's UI descriptor. It implements IUIModule to contribute seven navigation items, one invisible layout component, and its own assembly for Blazor component discovery.
    • Depends on: IUIModule, NavItem and NavSection from MMCA.Common.UI.Common, RoleNames, EngagementRoutePaths, LiveEventListener, MudBlazor Icons, and System.Reflection.
    • Concept, the pluggable UI module descriptor. [Rubric §18, UI Architecture] assesses how a modular monolith composes its front end without the host hard-coding each module's menu: every module ships an IUIModule, and the shared shell merges their nav items, layout components and assemblies (ADR-067). [Rubric §25, Navigation & IA]: the menu is declarative data here, not imperative wiring, including where each item sits: a Section, an optional Group key and an Order. [Rubric §11, Security]: four of the seven items pass RoleNames.Organizer as their required role (:39-42) so the shared NavMenu hides them from attendees; this is menu trimming, and the real enforcement remains the [Authorize(Roles = ...)] attribute on each page. [Rubric §27, i18n]: per the ADR-027 comment (:27-28), each Title and Group is a resource key, resolved by NavMenu against the co-located EngagementUIModule.resx pair at render time through the typeof(EngagementUIModule) title-resource pointer passed to every item, so the labels localize instead of being hard-coded English.
    • Walkthrough
      • Two group keys (:24-25): GroupConferenceDay = "Nav.Group.ConferenceDay" and GroupAttendeesAccess = "Nav.Group.AttendeesAccess". Per the class remarks (just above :22), the Administration groups are described once in ConferenceUIModule, which owns the organizer layout; this module only names their keys.
      • NavItems (:29-43) is a collection expression of seven entries, each pairing a resource key, a centralized route and an icon. Three sit in NavSection.User, the signed-in user section beside the profile entry: Nav.HappeningNow to HappeningNow (:33, Order = -90), Nav.MyPoints to MyPoints (:34, Order = -70) and Nav.MyBadge to MyBadge (:37, Order = -60). The negative orders sort them ahead of the framework's Notification Inbox (order 0), per the class remarks. The comment above HappeningNow (:31-32) gives the reason for the user section: the page is [Authorize], and the General section also renders for anonymous visitors, which offered them a link that only ends at the sign-in page; the comment above MyBadge (:36) says it is for every signed-in user because the badge page is also where an attendee links a ticket. Four sit in NavSection.Admin with the Organizer role: Nav.CheckIn to CheckInScan (:39, Conference day group, Order = 1), Nav.Attendance to OrganizerAttendance (:40, Conference day, Order = 2), Nav.PointsOverview to OrganizerPointsOverview (:41, Conference day, Order = 3), and Nav.TicketRoster to OrganizerTickets (:42, Attendees and access group, Order = 1).
      • LayoutComponentTypes (:45): [typeof(LiveEventListener)], an invisible component the shell renders on every page; the class summary says it joins the event live channel while the event is live.
      • Assembly (:47): typeof(EngagementUIModule).Assembly, so Blazor's router and component discovery can find this module's routable pages.
    • Why it's built this way: exposing nav, layout components and the assembly as read-only properties lets the host treat every module identically, and keeping the descriptor beside the routes it points at means adding a page is a two-line change in one project. Note what is deliberately absent: the two self-service QR routes (EngagementRoutePaths.cs:39-40) and the ticket insights route contribute no nav item, the first because they are reachable only by scanning a printed code, the second because it is reached from the roster page.
    • Where it's used: registered as a singleton IUIModule by DependencyInjection's AddEngagementUI (MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:90); consumed by the shared shell's NavMenu and router. The architecture suite's PermissionCoverageTests also reads it.

    DependencyInjection

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/DependencyInjection.cs:24 · Level 12 · class (static)

    • What it is: the Engagement UI composition root. One static class exposing an AddEngagementUI() extension on IServiceCollection that registers every Engagement UI service (bookmarks and their offline replay, reminders, feedback, check-in, points, tickets, lookups, the live layer, notification scoping) plus the EngagementUIModule descriptor.
    • Depends on: IServiceCollection and Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Extensions (for TryAddSingleton), the Engagement UI service interfaces and implementations, ISessionBookmarkUIService and ISessionLiveUIService from .Shared, the Common offline write queue (OfflineWriteQueue, IOfflineWriteHandler), and IUIModule plus INotificationScopeProvider from the Common UI framework.
    • Concept, extension(IServiceCollection) registration. [Rubric §5, Vertical Slice] and [Rubric §1, SOLID] assess whether a slice owns its own wiring: this is the single place the Engagement UI declares its services, so a host calls AddEngagementUI() and stays ignorant of the internals. The C# preview extension(IServiceCollection services) block (DependencyInjection.cs:26) is the DI-registration idiom used across the codebase (see the primer on extension(T) members), which is what lets AddEngagementUI read as an instance method on the collection.
    • Walkthrough: AddEngagementUI() (:32) registers in labelled groups, all scoped (per circuit) unless noted.
      • Bookmarks (:34-35): ISessionBookmarkUIService to SessionBookmarkUIService.
      • Offline bookmark toggles (:37-44): AddOfflineWriteQueue() (:42) plus one replay handler per queued kind, BookmarkCreateReplayHandler and BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler (:43-44). The comment (:37-41) records the scope of the guarantee: the queue is available on any host that registered a device store, and on a Blazor Server circuit the queued writes are kept in the browser's storage through JS interop, so the queue works only while the circuit is up (ADR-144).
      • SessionReminderCoordinator (:48), registered as a concrete type. The comment (ADR-042 Wave 2, :46-47) records that it keeps local notifications in sync with bookmarks and is a pure no-op on hosts whose local-notification service is unsupported.
      • Feedback (:50-53): IQuestionLookupService to QuestionLookupService, IEventFeedbackUIService to EventFeedbackService, ISessionFeedbackUIService to SessionFeedbackService.
      • Badge check-in (:55-57): ICheckInUIService to CheckInService, the one service behind the attendee badge, both organizer write paths and the attendance rollup.
      • Points (:59-61): IPointsUIService to PointsService.
      • Tickets (:63-65): ITicketUIService to TicketService, covering the organizer roster (upload, invites, funnel, delete) and the attendee's own tickets and barcode claim.
      • Cross-module lookups (:67-69): ISessionLookupService to SessionLookupService and IAttendeeLookupService to AttendeeLookupService, the two contracts the check-in surfaces use to name sessions and people that other services own.
      • Live layer (:71-74): ILivePollUIService, ILiveEventUIService, INowNextService; Wave 2 adds ISessionQuestionUIService and ISessionLiveUIService (:76-79).
      • Notification scoping (:81-87): services.TryAddSingleton(TimeProvider.System) then a plain AddScoped<INotificationScopeProvider, CurrentEventNotificationScopeProvider>(). Both lines carry load-bearing comments (:81-85): the plain AddScoped deliberately overrides the null provider that AddNotificationUI registers with TryAddScoped, so the two calls stay order-independent; and TimeProvider, which drives CurrentEventNotificationScopeProvider's cache expiry, is a TryAdd because AddOfflineWriteQueue above (and AddUIShared on the heads that call it) already registers the system clock.
      • Module descriptor (:89-90): AddSingleton<IUIModule, EngagementUIModule>(), a singleton because the descriptor is immutable metadata, while everything else is scoped since it holds per-circuit state.
      • Returns services (:92) for fluent chaining.
    • Why it's built this way: one extension method per module UI keeps registration cohesive and lets a host compose modules by convention. The TryAdd versus Add choices are the part worth reading closely: TryAdd where this module is a fallback provider (TimeProvider), plain Add where it must win over a framework default (the notification scope provider). [Rubric §29, Resilience, Reliability & Business Continuity]: getting that pair wrong is exactly how the notification bell would silently stop scoping to the current event.
    • Where it's used: called by the Blazor UI host's startup when the Engagement module is enabled, alongside the other modules' AddXUI() calls.

    • Depends on: the UserIdentifierType and SessionIdentifierType aliases. Externals: System.Globalization.
    • Concept introduced: the queue itself is taught at IOfflineWriteQueue. What these constants carry: a kind routes a queued write to its IOfflineWriteHandler, and is versioned (.v1) because a queued write can outlive an app update; a coalesce key names the writes that supersede one another, so one user's toggles of one session collapse to the newest intent.

The user is part of the key, so another user's toggle of the same session on a shared device never cancels this user's queued write.
    • Why it's built this way: the toggle service and both replay handlers must agree on these strings exactly, so they live once (ADR-144).
    • Where it's used: SessionBookmarkUIService (SessionBookmarkUIService.cs:91, :197-208), BookmarkCreateReplayHandler (BookmarkCreateReplayHandler.cs:32), BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler (BookmarkDeleteReplayHandler.cs:27).     SelfCheckInOutcome<TResult>

    MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI · MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI.Services.CheckIns · MMCA.ADC/Source/Modules/Engagement/MMCA.ADC.Engagement.UI/Services/CheckIns/SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:25 · Level 0 · sealed record (generic)

    • What it is: the return shape of one self-service check-in post, a sponsor booth visit or a room check-in. It carries the recorded payload, the server's stable error code, or a flag saying the attempt got no definitive answer at all, so the calling page can pick its state without catching an exception.
    • Depends on: nothing first-party; it is closed over SponsorVisitResultDTO and RoomCheckInResultDTO at the two call sites, and its ErrorCode values come from CheckInErrorCodes. Externals: BCL only, with a where TResult : class constraint (SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:26) so the nullable Value means exactly "absent".
    • Concept introduced, the result envelope for a refusal that is not a fault. [Rubric §1, SOLID] and [Rubric §9, API & Contract Design] both apply: the type doc (SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:3-13) explains that the landing pages must tell three server answers apart (no session running in this room, event not published, and the flat "unavailable" a disabled feature or unknown target produces), that all three arrive as ordinary non-success responses, and that two of them share the same 404 status. A result carrying only a message would force the page to parse localized prose; an exception would force a try/catch around a normal outcome. Carrying the code as data is what makes the page's mapping a switch expression over constants. The envelope also keeps a refusal apart from a non-answer: a rate limit, a timeout, a 5xx, a dropped network or a sign-in that could not be refreshed is not the server saying no, so it travels as IsTransient (param doc at SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:20-24) and the page offers a Retry instead of telling the attendee the code is not available. Note this is deliberately not the framework's Result, which the other four members of the same interface do return: this is a UI-layer transport envelope for one narrow HTTP pattern, so it stays small and local rather than reusing an abstraction whose error vocabulary it does not need.
    • Walkthrough (SelfCheckInOutcome.cs:25-29): three positional members, Value (the recorded outcome, null when the server refused), ErrorCode (null when the response carried none: a bare feature-gate 404 or an unparseable body, per the param doc at :16-19) and IsTransient, which defaults to false (:25) so every refusal construction stays a two-argument call and only the no-answer branches name the flag. One computed member, IsSuccess => Value is not null (:29), so success is derived from the payload rather than tracked as a further field that could disagree with it. Construction is centralized in CheckInService.PostSelfCheckInAsync (CheckInService.cs:172-208): the success branch deserializes TResult and pairs it with a null code (:178-182); a 401 still standing after the refresh attempt, or a retryable status still standing after the in-place retries, returns IsTransient: true (:184-187), as do a transport failure (:191-194) and an HttpClient timeout, which surfaces as a cancellation the caller never requested (:195-200); any other non-success passes null with whatever ReadErrorCodeAsync extracted from the RFC 9457 problem body (:189, defined at :393-428).
    • Why it's built this way: the four other members on the same service run through HttpResultExecutor.ExecuteAsync and answer with a framework Result (CheckInService.cs:55-70, :108-124, :131-146), because an organizer facing a broken scan wants a typed failure to surface. The two attendee-facing self-service writes must not, because every refusal is a sentence the landing page renders calmly to someone holding a phone in a hallway, and an unanswered attempt is a Retry button rather than a refusal. The method doc records both rules (CheckInService.cs:155-171). Keeping the generic on the payload lets one private helper serve both endpoints with no duplication (ADR-072).
    • Where it's used: returned by ICheckInUIService.RecordSponsorVisitAsync and .RecordRoomCheckInAsync (ICheckInUIService.cs:58, :70), implemented at CheckInService.cs:85 and :97, consumed by SponsorVisit (SponsorVisit.razor.cs:98, mapping IsTransient to VisitState.Transient at :112) and RoomCheckIn (RoomCheckIn.razor.cs:87, mapping it to CheckInState.Transient at :110). Page-tested through SponsorVisitTests and RoomCheckInTests.
